- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, reduce forecast slope if true outcome shows early correction or mean reversion.
- If supply net is heavily negative (e.g., -10+ events/30d) and model forecasts remain flat or rising, adjust downward by 3–5% to account for bearish sentiment and supply shock.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model forecasts often overshoot; cap forecast growth to 1–2% per day post-spike to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67/0.00 alternation), model should not assume linear trend; apply smoothing or lagged decay to avoid overfitting.
- When official events are clustered (e.g., 3+ auctions in 5 days), model should reduce forecast momentum; treat as “event-driven volatility” and cap forecast rise to 1.5% per event.
- If true outcome deviates from forecast by >5% in first 3 days, reset forecast baseline to true outcome’s 3-day moving average to avoid lagged bias.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤0.33), apply downward bias of 2–4% to account for policy uncertainty or supply shock.
- If model forecasts are rising while sentiment is flat or bearish, reduce forecast slope by 50% to avoid overconfidence in bullish signals.
